reason: The cited evidence (E2) suggests that Cu could play a structural role and maintain magnetic entropy change in a different alloy system (NiFeCoCr-based HEAs), but it provides no direct support for the key premises regarding grain boundary segregation, mechanical property improvement, or the specific retention of magnetocaloric effect in MnNiSi-based materials. E1 is a general background on MCE and does not address the premises.
premises: Cu addition will segregate at grain boundaries and reduce internal stresses, improving ductility and fatigue resistance.
Cu is largely non-magnetic and plays a dominantly structural role, so it will minimally perturb the magneto-structural transition.
Minor FCC metal additions (like Cu) can tune microstructure and improve mechanical properties in related systems.
The magnetocaloric effect (ΔSM) will be retained within ~10% of the undoped material.
